gloss: to always have a comeback; to be quick-tongued

definitions.gloss: to always have a comeback; to be quick-tongued; to never be at a loss for words
definitions.explanation: Describes someone who always has something to say in response, especially excuses or cheeky replies. Usually said with mild exasperation or disapproval about someone who talks back no matter what.

examples.japanese: ⟦{本当|ほんとう}→本当：00779_hontou⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{口|くち}が{減|へ}らない⟦やつ→やつ：10782_yatsu⟧だ。
⟦{叱|しか}って→叱る：01202_shikaru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧{口|くち}が{減|へ}らない⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{焼|や}いている→焼く：01123_yaku⟧。
examples.english: I'm having trouble with a child who always has a comeback no matter how much I scold them.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{後輩|こうはい}→後輩：02501_kouhai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{口|くち}が{減|へ}らなくて、⟦{先輩|せんぱい}→先輩：01451_senpai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{注意|ちゅうい}→注意：01464_chuui⟧⟦されて→する：00392_suru⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{言|い}い{訳|わけ}→言い訳：04653_iiwake⟧⟦ばかり→〜ばかり：02006_bakari⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: That junior always has a retort — even when a senior warns him, he just makes excuses.

notes:
USAGE:
An idiomatic expression with a negative connotation. Used when someone is being criticized or confronted but keeps talking back instead of accepting the criticism. The literal meaning is 'the mouth doesn't decrease' — i.e., they never run out of words.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {口|くち}が{減|へ}らない⟦やつ→やつ：10782_yatsu⟧ (a person who always talks back)
- {口|くち}が{減|へ}らない⟦{子|こ}→子：09851_ko⟧ (a child who always has something to say)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{口達者|くちだっしゃ}→口達者：15420_kuchidassha⟧: eloquent/smooth-talking — can be neutral or positive, while {口|くち}が{減|へ}らない is always mildly negative
- ⟦{減|へ}らず{口|ぐち}→減らず口：07396_herazuguchi⟧: back talk, cheeky retort — the noun form of the same concept
